pages.text: Drop a ball through rows of pegs. At each it goes left or right with even odds, so after n rows it has gone right k times with probability C(n,k)/2ⁿ. Pile up enough balls and the binomial heap becomes a bell curve: $(thing)the central limit theorem$().

The $(item)Galton Board$() sorts raw ore into ingots by where each piece lands after 12 rows: within one of the middle, one ingot (61%); two or three away, two (35%); four or more, three (4%). On average 1.43 ingots a piece.
